hints: Look closely at rows 1 to 4 and ask yourself, can one single virus particle carry both DNA and RNA at the same time?
Remember the golden virus rule for 9700: each virus has either DNA or RNA as its genetic material, never both and never neither.
walkthrough:
**Recall what a virus must contain**

Think of a virus particle as a tiny parcel of genetic instructions wrapped in protein. That instruction must be either DNA or RNA, so it can be copied inside a host cell.

Rule to remember: 1 virus = 1 type of nucleic acid.

**Check each row against the rule**

Row 1 has both DNA and RNA present, so no single virus can look like this. Row 4 has neither DNA nor RNA, so it has no genetic material at all and cannot be a virus.

That leaves Row 2 (DNA only) as a DNA virus, and Row 3 (RNA only) as an RNA virus.

**Pick the pair of two different viruses**

The question asks for two different virus particles in the air sample. We need one DNA virus and one RNA virus. That is exactly rows 2 and 3.

options.A: Row 1 is impossible because no virus contains both DNA and RNA together, so 1 and 2 cannot both be correct.
options.B: Row 1 is impossible for the same reason, even though row 3 is a valid RNA virus.
options.C: Row 2 shows a DNA-only virus and row 3 shows an RNA-only virus, which perfectly matches two different viruses.
options.D: Row 4 is impossible because every virus must contain some nucleic acid, so a particle with neither DNA nor RNA is not a virus.
